70627.subject: Literature in English
70627.question_text:
This question is based on Literary Appreciation.

Football is the only sport on earth that can be considered truly global. Simple and inexpensive. it is equally likely to be found in a tight Marseille banlieue, an obscure corner of a Lagos slum, and the heart of a Buenos barrio. Marley's music is similarly universal...

According to the excerpt above, football is
70627.explanation:
The writer says that Football is the only sport that is truly global as it can be found anywhere in the world. The writer compares football to Marley's music. He says "Marley's music is similarly universal..."

The use of the conjunction "but" in option C, makes the sentiment different from that of the writer. The writer makes use of the word "inexpensive" instead of cheap to avoid the negative connotation attached to the word "cheap".

70628.subject: Literature in English
70628.question_text:
This question is based on Literary Appreciation.

"The commission has the power to investigate, 
to conciliate to hold hearings, to order
reinstatement of a discharged employee, and
to direct the appointment of a qualified applicant"

The rhetorical device used in the excerpt above is
70628.explanation: Parallelism is the repetition of similar grammatical constructions through a line of literary work for rhetorical effect. The repetition of the construction "to ..." as in "to investigate,/ to conciliate, to hold hearings, to order..." helps to achieve that rhetorical effect and to make the poem more memorable to the audience.

70630.subject: Literature in English
70630.question_text:
This question is based on Alex Agyei-Agyiri's Unexpected Joy at Dawn.

The setting of the novel is
70630.explanation: The novel is set in  Ghana and Nigeria, with the immediate space in Accra, Ghana while more of the events in the latter take place in Lagos, Illere and Ijase. The setting alternates between the countries.

70631.subject: Literature in English
70631.question_text:
This question is based on Alex Agyei-Agyiri's Unexpected Joy at Dawn.

Wachuk in the novel is
70631.explanation: Wachuk is Idem's husband. He works at a printing press in Mafoluku.

70632.subject: Literature in English
70632.question_text: In Senghor's Black Woman, the dominant literary device is
70632.explanation: In "Black Woman" by Leopold Sedar Senghor, the dominant literary device is metaphor. Senghor frequently compares the black woman to abstract and natural elements, such as the earth, the sun and a divine presence, to celebrate her beauty, strength and cultural significance. These metaphor are central to the poem's themes of identity and appreciation of African heritage.

70633.subject: Literature in English
70633.question_text: Sesay's "The Song of the Woman of My Land" is a
70633.explanation: A panegyric poem is a poem that formally praises someone or something publicly. Oumar Farouk Sesay's "The Song of the Women of My Land" is written to recognise the efforts of the women in colonial Sierra Leone. He praises them for their resilience despite the harsh and oppressive conditions that they faced.

70634.subject: Literature in English
70634.question_text: In Eliot's "Journey of the Magi", "six hands at an open door" is an example of
70634.explanation: In T.S. Eliot's "Journey of the Magi," the phrase "six hands at an open door" uses synecdoche, a figure of speech in which a part represents a whole or a whole represents a part. Here, "six hands" refers to three people (in this case, the Magi on the journey).

70635.subject: Literature in English
70635.explanation:
Niyi Osundare's "The Leader and the Led" is a satiric poem as it is written to mock the leaders and followers in post-colonial Africa, particularly Nigeria. He compares the leaders to various animals to provide vivid descriptions of the failures of our African leaders who put their selfish interests above all else.

Osundare mocks the leaders and followers in post-colonial Africa with the aim of correcting them.

70636.subject: Literature in English
70636.question_text: The poet persona in Donne's "The Good Morrow" reflects on
70636.explanation:
One of the major ideas expressed in John Donne's "The Good Morrow" is that true love will never die. Other types of love may prove to be temporary, but true love will stand the test of time. We find this idea in the third stanza of the poem, where the poet's persona states: 'My face in thine eyes,/ thine in mine appears/ And true plain hearts do in the faces rest." Their love for each other shows in their eyes.

Furthermore, the poet's persona refers to himself and his lover as "two hemispheres" and claims that "whatever dies was not mixed equally;/ if two lovers be one, or, thou and I/ Love so alike, that none do slacken, none can die." Here, he states that both of them are not only halves of one entity but a complete union of two souls. Their love will never die because their love is not a mere union of bodies; it is a union of souls. All of these portray the immortality of their love.

70637.subject: Literature in English
70637.question_text: The style of Chibuike's "A Government Driver on His Retirement" is
70637.explanation: One Chibuike's "A Government Driver on His Retirement" is a narrative poem. It narrates the tragic story of a government driver on the day of his retirement. He chooses to celebrate with alcohol after years of being sober and carefully to his duties. However, he drinks too much and he heads home in his car. This intoxication is what leads to his tragic death. The poem teaches the devastating impact of intoxication and poor decisions and how it can undo all the good that we have done.

70638.subject: Literature in English
70638.question_text:
"But a caged bird stands on the grave of dreams"

The excerpt above from Angelou's "Caged Bird" implies that caged bird
70638.explanation: In Maya Angelou's "Caged Bird". the line "But a caged bird stands on the grave of dreams" symbolises the frustration and despair of being trapped, with no freedom to pursue one's aspirations. The "grave of dreams" suggests that the bird's hopes and desires are buried, unattainable due to its confinement. This imagery conveys a sense of deep frustration rather than literal death or freedom.

options.text: walks freely to actualise its dream

70639.subject: Literature in English
70639.explanation: D.H Lawrence's "Bats" is a dramatic monologue in which the speaker shares personal observations and emotions about bats. It blends vivid imagery with subjective reflection to capture the speaker's changing perspective on the creatures. It begins with admiration, then confusion, then discomfort and finally disgust.

70640.subject: Literature in English
70640.question_text:
This question is based on Wole Soyinka's The Lion and the Jewel

Lakunle declines to pay bride price on Sidi because he sees tradition as
70640.explanation: Lakunle declines to pay bride price on Sidi because he sees the tradition as barbaric. Lakunle labels the culture that persists on a bride price being paid before a man can marry a woman as "a savage custom, barbaric, outdated" (p. 7)

70643.subject: Literature in English
70643.question_text:
The question is based on Wole Soyinka's The Lion and the Jewel

The play is a
70643.explanation: Wole Soyinka's The Lion and the Jewel is a comedy that uses humour and witty dialogue to explore themes such as tradition versus modernity, gender roles and cultural identity.While the play addresses social issues, its tone remains light-hearted and the resolution involves no tragic consequences. This makes it a comedic work.

70644.subject: Literature in English
70644.question_text:
This question is based on John Osborne's Look Back in Anger

Alison and Jimmy are accommodated during the first month of their marriage by
70644.explanation: Hugh Tanner is Jimmy's friend who took Alison and Jimmy into his apartment in the first months of their marriage. He was Jimmy's partner when they went on "raids" against Allison's upper-class friends at fancy parties, and Jimmy saw him as a co-conspirator in the class struggle.

70645.subject: Literature in English
70645.question_text:
This question is based on John Osbourne's Look Back in Anger

The protagonist in the play is
70645.explanation: The protagonist of John Osbourne's Look Back in Anger is Jimmy Porter. The drama revolves around his unhappy marriage with Alison and his hatred of the upper-class, older generation of English men.

70646.subject: Literature in English
70646.question_text:
This question is based on John Osbourne's Look Back in Anger

The couple's marital crisis is aggravated by
70646.explanation: In John Osbourne's Look Back in Anger, Helena Charles, Alison's friend, plays a significant role in aggravating the couple's marital crisis. She not only influences Allison to leave Jimmy but also becomes romantically involved with him after Alison's departure.

70647.subject: Literature in English
70647.question_text:
This question is based on John Osborne's Look Back in Anger.

The reason why Jimmy easily gets along with Cliff is because
70647.explanation: In Osborne's Look Back in Anger, Jimmy and Cliff share a close bond because they both come from working-class backgrounds. This shared experience fosters mutual understanding and camaraderie, in contrast to the tension between Jimmy and Alison, who comes from an upper-class family.

options.text: they both belong to the working class
the relatives of Jimmy's mother are rich
they are both from affluent backgrounds

70648.subject: Literature in English
70648.question_text:
This question is based on John Osborne's Look Back in Anger.

Jimmy's harmatia is
70648.explanation: In John Osborne's Look Back in Anger, Jimmy's hamartia (tragic flaw) is his uncontrolled anger and bitterness toward society, class structures, and those around him. His constant outbursts and inability to express his emotions constructively create rifts in his relationships, especially with Alison.

70649.subject: Literature in English
70649.question_text:
This question is based on Buchi Emecheta's Second Class Citizen

Adah is so obsessed with the sleek woman at the hospital because the woman
70649.explanation: In Buchi Emecheta's Second Class Citizen, Adah admires and becomes obsessed with the sleek woman at the hospital because the woman has a caring and loving husband. This contrasts sharply with Adah's own troubled married to Francis. The sleek woman is "showered with presents of flowers, funny dolls that made mad music, beautiful boxes... that contained all sorts of things" (pg. 124) and it never occurs to Adah that "such things could be real" (p. 125).

70650.subject: Literature in English
70650.question_text:
This question is based on Buchi Emecheta's Second Class Citizen.

Adah's disappointment is in the overwhelming
70650.explanation: Adah's disappointment stems from the racial discrimination she experiences and observes in England. Despite her high hopes for equality and better opportunities.she is confronted with the harsh realities of being treated as inferior due to her race and status as an immigrant.

70651.subject: Literature in English
70651.question_text:
This question is based on Buchi Emecheta's Second Class Citizen

The main challenge Adah encounters in England is
70651.explanation:
"you may be living like an elite but the day you land in England, you are a second-class citizen" (pg. 43). This is what Francis reminds his wife of when she lands in England and questions the terrible apartment that Francis had secured for them. 

In their desire to find a new abode, husband and wife have to contend with discrimination because of the colour of their skin. "Her house-hunting was made more difficult because she was black." In some places where there is a vacant room, "nearly all notices had 'Sorry, no coloureds' on them" (p. 76). Gradually, she learns that "her colour was something she was supposed to be ashamed of" (p. 76).

70652.subject: Literature in English
70652.question_text:
The question is based on Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights

The structure of the novel is based on two major conflicts of
70652.explanation: In Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights, the structure of the novel revolves around two major conflicts driven by passion. The intense, consuming love between Heathcliff and Catherine is the central force that shapes the narrative. Their passion leads to destructive consequences for themselves and those around them.

70653.subject: Literature in English
70653.question_text:
This question is based on Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights

The setting of the novel is
70653.explanation: Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights is set in mid-18th century England. The novel takes place over several generations with the main events unfolding in the years following the late 1700s.

70654.subject: Literature in English
70654.question_text:
This question is based on Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights

The novel can be described as a
70654.explanation:
Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights is a Victorian novel. It was published during the Victorian era (1847). Like most Victorian novels, it:

1. Explores the issue of class and the social hierarchy. Characters like Heathcliff struggle against the constraints of their social class.

2. It explores the human psyche. The novel's characters are emotionally intense, with Heathcliff and Catherine's obsessive love and inner turmoil being central to the narrative. 

3. It contains Gothic elements, such as the supernatural and the darker aspects of human nature

70655.subject: Literature in English
70655.question_text:
This question is based on Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights.

Heathcliff considered himself the second half of
70655.explanation: Heathcliff considers himself the second half of Catherine Earnshaw. In Wuthering Heights, Heathcliff and Catherine share a deep, obsessive connection and Heathcliff believes that they are two halves of a whole.

70656.subject: Literature in English
70656.question_text:
This question is based on General Literary Principles.

The collection of images within a literary work is referred to as
70656.explanation: Imagery is the use of vivid and descriptive language that appeals to the senses and creates pictures in the minds of the readers. It is a collection of images that enhance the meaning or emotional effect of the work.

70657.subject: Literature in English
70657.question_text:
This question is based on general literary principles

The leading character in a literary work is the
70657.explanation: The protagonist is the leading character in a literary work. He is the one who faces the central conflict and whose actions drive the plot forward.

70658.subject: Literature in English
70658.question_text: A long narrative poem that relates heroic exploits is
70658.explanation: An epic is a long narrative poem that recounts the heroic exploits of a central figure or group, often involving grand events or adventures.

70659.subject: Literature in English
70659.question_text:
This question is based on General Literary Principles.

A poem of eight rhyming lines is
70659.explanation: A poem of eight rhyming lines is an octave.

70660.subject: Literature in English
70660.question_text:
This question is based on General Literary Principles.

The events that make up the story is the
70660.explanation: The plot is the sequence of events that make up a story, including the conflict, rising action, climax, falling action and resolution. It is the structure that organises the events and actions in the narrative.
